records.text: Owens said former British banker and whistleblower Simon Andriesz, previously a managing director at BGC Group where Howard Lutnick was CEO, had died in what was being described as a suicide after allegedly flagging Lutnick’s Epstein connections and saying some money laundering was happening.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This was a person who was blowing the whistle on Howard Lutnick. And I will say allegedly here, a lot of people just when they are telling the story about Jeffrey Epstein, the Jeffrey Epstein network, it just a lot of suicides happen and we've had another suicide here is the headline, the banker whistleblower who who flagged Howard Lutnick's links to Epstein (Jeffrey Epstein) dies. ... A former British banker and a whistleblower, his name was Simon Andres (banker whistleblower; transcript name spelling unverified), and he essentially came forward. He was previously a managing director at Wall Street firm BGC Group, where Lutnick (Howard Lutnick), who is now the U.S. Commerce Secretary, was the CEO. ... OK, and so he's now dead after he was saying, hey, there was some money laundering that was happening and he was also behind the push to notify people.

records.text: According to Owens’s account of his BBC remarks, Simon Andriesz said he found evidence that Howard Lutnick failed to disclose a business relationship with Epstein, including a 2018 email chain discussing prospects for a startup in which Lutnick and Epstein were both involved.
